items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-04
items.q: Because tonight I played against Earl Hines down there. And Earl Hines had a good band in them days.

ctx.x: Well, when you had a contest, would the other band play the same tune or what? How would that work?

No, no. They'd play what they want. They'd play what they wanted. They'd play the best they got. They'd play what they wanted to. You don't have to play just what they play. Sometimes accidentally you play a number they played already, or they're going to play, something like that. But you don't have to play. You just play what you think you can play best. Best super for your band, that's what you play. Because tonight I played against Earl Hines down there. And Earl Hines had a good band in them days. He was a…

take me a couple of shots and I begin to call some numbers. I'll begin to blow a little bit. Take me a couple of more shots. And just give me that drum, that piano, and bass. Then I'll get the people over here. Just clap your hand, I'll bring the people here. Well around 1.30 I had Earl Hines over there, let alone all the people. Had him over there. Him and his whole band, because I know that boy was playing first alto with him, I knew him better. He's a fine guy, he played violin too.
